title: Oriental Cork Oak: Ancient Oriental Cork Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: A sacred oak in Yabu, 5.6 metres round and near 400 years old, a Seoul oak said to be a general's walking stick, and Utah's state champion.
intro: One of our oriental cork oaks is said to be a general's walking stick, one is a home of the gods, and one is a state record. The species is an East Asian oak whose bark thickens into deep corky ridges, although the cork in a wine bottle comes from a different oak in the western Mediterranean. The biggest grows on a mountainside behind a former school in Yabu, Japan, where the district treats the tree itself as sacred, with no shrine around it. The national register, which made it a Natural Monument in 1951, records 5.6 metres round, about 16 metres tall and an age near 400 years. In Seoul, legend says one grew from the cane of General Gang Gam-chan, the commander who crushed a Khitan invasion in 1019, but the survey made before its designation in 1982 put it at roughly 250 years. And on the University of Utah campus, the state's Big Tree Register measured one in 2026 at 19.8 metres tall and named it Utah's champion.
